data.title: Process
data.tagline: A process is a running program together with the separate resource environment assigned by the operating system.
data.learningOutcome: You can use process IDs and memory isolation to identify separate processes and verify whether one keeps working after another exits.
data.description: A web server and image worker can run as separate processes with different process IDs and isolated memory. If the image worker crashes, it can restart independently while the web process keeps serving. A process is neither a program file nor a whole machine; one machine can run many processes.

learning.assumes: You know a service keeps running in the operating system after it starts.
learning.outcome: You can use process IDs and memory isolation to identify separate processes and verify whether one keeps working after another exits.

distinctions.label: Thread
distinctions.explanation: A Process is the isolated OS resource allocation unit; a Thread is an execution unit inside a process sharing its memory space.

explanation.title: Problem and key mechanism
explanation.text: When web requests and image work share one process, an image-worker crash can stop the site; send image jobs to a separate process through a queue or pipe so the OS manages resources and exit states separately and the failure returns to job status.

explanation.title: Verify the failure boundary
explanation.text: Crash the image process and confirm the web process still responds while the job fails or retries. Communication and durable state still need design.

explanation.title: Code editors also separate processes
explanation.text: A code editor can run its language analyzer in a separate process. If the analyzer crashes, the editor can still save files and restart only the analyzer.

data.boundary: A process is a running execution environment, not a program file or an entire machine. Isolation can limit crashes and memory impact, but inter-process communication, persistence, and recovery remain separate concerns.

lessonPractice.title: Image work uses lots of memory and sometimes crashes inside the web process. Which change creates process isolation?

options.label: Run image work in a separate process and record both PIDs and exit states
options.feedback: Correct. The image process can exit and restart independently while the web process is checked for continued service.

options.label: Move image code to another function but call it in the same process
options.feedback: A function boundary does not isolate process resources or lifecycle.

options.label: Rename the same process image-service while it still handles web requests
options.feedback: A name does not create a runtime boundary; inspect PIDs, memory, and lifecycle.

data.agentPrompt: Move image processing into a separate process that receives work through a queue or pipe. Record the web and image PIDs, memory, and exit states. Crash the image process and verify web requests still work while the image job becomes visibly failed or retryable.
